title: Measure provision

blocks.heading: Measure provision
blocks.text: Literacy, school enrolment and tertiary participation describe different aspects of educational provision. Use age group, denominator and period consistently. Enrolment is not attendance, completion or learning quality, and a larger count can reflect a larger eligible population.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Literacy
blocks.text: A literacy measure identifies reading and writing ability under the source’s stated definition and population. Compare the same age and measurement rules. A national average can hide group or regional gaps and does not measure every skill.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: School enrolment
blocks.text: Primary and secondary enrolment counts show participation registered at those levels. Compare counts with eligible populations or capacity and keep levels separate. More registered learners do not establish regular attendance or adequate teaching.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Tertiary enrolment
blocks.text: Tertiary enrolment measures participation in post-secondary institutions under the source’s definition. A rising total can indicate expansion while its rate remains unchanged if the eligible population grows similarly. Access, course relevance and completion need separate evidence.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Apply the distinction
blocks.text: Describe the provision relationship in this original fictional comparison: A registers 300 of 500 eligible school children; B registers 240 of 300. A has more enrolled children but B the higher rate, 80% versus 60%. Counts and coverage give different rankings.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Connect the ideas
blocks.text: Connect to Health (7.2), modern roles (6.2) and Development (1.1). Separate access, participation and learning outcomes; do not assume a system label or device purchase establishes quality.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
